items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: Oh, I played with Sharky many times. Yes, many, many, many times.

ctx.x: Was Sharky, did you also play with Sharky?
Oh, I played with Sharky many times. Yes, many, many, many times.
Of course, he went to, he took Bix's place in the Wolverines.

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: Well, I think some of the sessions that I made with Sharky were very good from a real Dixieland standpoint.

ctx.x: No, I don't believe accurately. I've tried to put it across on some of the recordings. The album that I made here at the Gollywog that has never been released, I think, contains more of this than anything else that I've ever done. But it's been most unfortunate that it's never been released. And in this album, I attempted more styles, different things that I've ever done before. In fact, I did a lot of Royal Heinz, Teddy Wilson, George Shearing, Jess Stacey, Errol Garner. In fact, I tried to cover practically…

Mm-hmm. Speaking of records, what about records with bands where you function as a sideman, with any sessions that you think, either from your point of view or as a whole were more outstanding than others that you can think of offhand?
Well, I think some of the sessions that I made with Sharky were very good from a real Dixieland standpoint.

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: Yeah, well you know, it was one of those things, you see, when Deck of Records came through, they wanted Sharky, so naturally I guess he picked out a band that he thought would be better suited for jazz records.

ctx.x: And you didn't use the same guy?

He didn't use the same band, no. That's funny. Yeah, well you know, it was one of those things, you see, when Deck of Records came through, they wanted Sharky, so naturally I guess he picked out a band that he thought would be better suited for jazz records. And I guess that's the way it went. You had Leo Brookhoven, you say? Leo Brookhoven playing trumpet, Fitch trumpet. And of course we had a full saxophone section, a fellow by the name of Scorsoni playing sax, and Franzella played sax a while out there. And we…
